review_title: Surgical methods for first trimester termination of pregnancy
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion were eligible.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset label 1.0 counts as INCLUDE; 0.5 and 0.0 count as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Early complication after induced first‐trimaster abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This is an observational study analyzing complications in 5,851 consecutively induced first-trimester abortions. It does not compare different surgical methods and is not a randomised controlled trial. The study examines risk factors for complications rather than comparing surgical techniques.

studies.study_title: Manual vacuum aspiration, a safe and effective alternative in early pregnancy termination
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing conventional vacuum aspiration (VA) with manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for first trimester abortion (gestational age less than 56 days). 200 women were randomized to VA or MVA, meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Induced termination of pregnancy before and after Roe v Wade. Trends in the mortality and morbidity of women
studies.predicted_reason: This is a historical/trend analysis using data from national health statistics and surveillance systems. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not compare surgical methods. The study examines mortality and morbidity trends over time periods.

While this is a randomised controlled trial, it compares cervical preparation methods (prostaglandin suppository vs placebo) rather than different surgical methods. All women in both groups received vacuum aspiration as the surgical method. The intervention being tested is pre-operative cervical preparation, not the surgical technique itself.

studies.study_title: A comparison of D&C and vacuum aspiration for performing first trimester abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing dilatation and curettage (D&C) with vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion. 420 women were randomly assigned to D&C or vacuum aspiration at 6-12 weeks gestation, meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Acceptability of manual versus electric aspiration for first trimester abortion: a randomised trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration with electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion. 84 women were randomized to manual or electric vacuum aspiration at less than 10 weeks gestation, meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Similarities in women's perception and acceptability of manual vacuum aspiration and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion.
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) with electric vacuum aspiration (EVA) for first trimester abortion. Women were randomly assigned to MVA (n=64) or EVA (n=63), meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Abortion by means of suction curettage compared to conventional metal curette
studies.predicted_reason: While this study compares vacuum aspiration with dilatation and curettage for first trimester abortion, the abstract does not explicitly state that women were randomised to the treatment groups. It describes a comparative study of 47 women (23 vacuum aspiration, 24 D&C) but lacks clear evidence of randomised allocation. Without confirmation of randomisation, this cannot be confirmed as meeting the RCT criterion.

studies.study_title: First trimester abortion by vacuum aspiration
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing two types of cannulae (8mm metal vs flexible plastic) for vacuum aspiration in first trimester abortion. 300 subjects were randomly assigned to receive one of the two cannula types at 7-10 weeks gestation. This compares variations in surgical technique within the vacuum aspiration method.

studies.study_title: Comparison of pain and time of procedure with two first trimester abortion techniques performed by residents and faculty
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspirator with electric vacuum curettage for first trimester abortion. 114 women were randomized to receive one of the two surgical techniques, meeting all selection criteria.
